subject: "Null verb" in the grammar of graphics?

messages.author: b3204ecc9b0f3f36
messages.subject: "Null verb" in the grammar of graphics?
parts:
I'm working on a package "ggress" that will allow progressive ggplot graphs in an rmd ioslides presentation. That is to say, just as you can currently set ioslides to show just one bullet point at a time, I'm making something to make it easy to do things like showing one line at a time in a graph. In order to do this, I want to have it so something like:

```
ggress(1:2, ggplot(mtcars,aes(y=mpg,x=wt)) + geom_point() + since(2,geom_smooth()))
```

evaluates to something like:

```
cat("<div class='build'>\n")
cat("  <div>")
ggplot(mtcars,aes(y=mpg,x=wt)) + geom_point() + null_verb()
cat("  </div>")
cat("  <div>")
ggplot(mtcars,aes(y=mpg,x=wt)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth()
cat("  </div>")
cat("</div>")
```

But I don't know what to put in null_verb. I'm sure I could figure it out if I dived deep enough into the ggplot codebase but I also imagine somebody here can answer it easily.

Thanks,
Jameson

(ps. I was in the Harvard class that Hadley talked to last Friday. I asked the first question, about the possibility of an R coffeescript-like thing, and his answer to that question and to the later one about Julia were convincing enough to a doubting Thomas like me to inspire me to try to do this rather than something else. So, great job, Hadley.)
